name: Ace of Swords
symbols: A hand from a cloud holds a sword upright — clarity, given.
A crown on the sword's tip — truth, with authority.
A laurel and a palm branch — victory, but the victory of sight.
Clouds around the hilt — the clarity emerges from what has been unclear.

reading.upright: The Ace of Swords is the breakthrough of clarity: a truth that cuts through, a decision that can now be made, a seeing that was not possible before.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the clarity fails: confusion, miscommunication, or a sword drawn too quickly and cutting the wrong thing.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the sword, the clouds, the crown)
elementalRegister.note: The Ace of Swords is the root of the air suit: the breakthrough of clarity, the sword of truth that cuts through confusion.

numericalDegree.note: The Ace is the root of the suit, the seed of the element. It is the degree of pure potential, before the number has begun to differentiate.

courtFunction.note: The Ace is not a court card; it is the elemental root of the suit.

figureType.value: A hand from a cloud, holding a sword upright
figureType.note: The hand is the only figure. It comes from the cloud, marking the clarity as a gift from beyond the self.

posture.value: The hand holds the sword upright
posture.note: The upright posture of the sword is the posture of clarity: the blade is held aloft, ready to cut through.

gesture.value: Holding the sword upright, with a crown on its tip
gesture.note: The gesture is one of offering and authority. The sword is held aloft, crowned with truth.

gaze.note: There is no gaze. The Ace is not a personality; it is a force.

movementDirection.note: There is no directional movement. The Ace is the point of clarity, not the journey.

centralObject.note: The sword is the instrument of clarity; the crown is the mark of truth's authority. Both are the symbols of the card's breakthrough.

heldObject.note: The sword is held by the hand from the cloud. It is the gift of the element.

creature.note: There is no creature. The Ace is the pure element, before it has taken animal form.

tool.note: The tool is the sword, the instrument of the air suit.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The Ace's law is the clarity itself, not a written instruction.

landscape.note: The landscape is the sky, the realm of air. It is the world of clarity and thought.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The Ace is in the open, at the source of the air.

threshold.note: The cloud is the threshold between the unseen and the seen. The hand emerges from it, bringing the clarity into the world.

celestialBody.note: The clouds are the celestial source of the gift. The clarity comes from above, not from the earth.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The Ace is the clear moment of breakthrough.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the hand from the side, the sword upright)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The Ace is a point of departure, not a balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number one is the number of the breakthrough. The Ace is the single point of clarity.

verticalAxis.value: The sword upright, the hand from above
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the celestial (the cloud) to the earthly (the sword). The sword is the point of connection.

horizontalAxis.value: The sword held to the side
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the offering: the sword is held out, available to be taken.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The Ace is upright and clear.

clothing.note: There is no clothing. The Ace is the bare element, without the mediation of culture.

nudity.note: There is no body. The Ace is the element itself, not a person.

crown.value: A crown on the sword's tip
crown.note: The crown is the mark of truth's authority. It is a crown of clarity, not of social rank.

wound.note: There is no wound. The Ace is pure potential, not yet marked by experience.

binding.note: There are no chains. The clarity is free.

water.note: There is no water. The Ace of Swords is the root of air.

fire.note: There is no fire. The Ace of Swords is the root of air.

vegetation.note: The laurel and palm are the marks of victory, the victory of sight.

stone.note: There is no stone. The Ace is the element of air, not of earth.

polarity.note: The Ace of Swords' remedy-pair is the Ace of Pentacles: air and earth, clarity and grounding. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Ace of Swords' clarity is the Ace of Pentacles' grounding: sometimes the clarity needs to be corrected by the material commitment.

prescribedAct.value: Say the one true thing today that you have been avoiding, and let it cut through.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of clarity. The Ace of Swords' lesson is that the truth is a blade that must be drawn.

detailedReading: The Ace of Swords is the root of the air suit: the breakthrough of clarity, the sword of truth that cuts through confusion. Its elemental register is air, and its numerical degree is the Ace, the seed of the element. The figure is a hand from a cloud, holding a sword upright, with a crown on its tip and laurel and palm branches. The landscape is the sky, the realm of air. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the Ace is the pure element, free and open. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a point of departure. The prescribed act follows from this: say the one true thing today that you have been avoiding, and let it cut through. The remedy is grounding — the Ace of Pentacles — because the clarity needs to be corrected by the material commitment.

name: Two of Swords
symbols: A blindfolded figure holds two swords crossed — the choice, avoided by not looking.
The sea behind her — emotion, present but not the deciding factor.
A crescent moon — intuition, available but not consulted.
The stance is balanced — the stalemate is stable, and that is the problem.

reading.upright: The Two of Swords is the stalemate: a difficult choice not yet made, a balance achieved by not looking.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the stalemate breaks: either the decision arrives, or the overload of information makes it impossible.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the crossed swords, the blindfold)
elementalRegister.note: The Two of Swords is the air element in its phase of stalemate. The blindfolded figure marks it as the card of the choice avoided.

numericalDegree.note: Two is the number of polarity and choice. The card is the moment at which the single clarity of the Ace becomes the contested pair.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Two is the first differentiation of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A blindfolded standing human figure, holding two crossed swords
figureType.note: The figure is human and blindfolded. Her blindfold marks the card as one of the choice avoided by not looking.

posture.value: Standing, arms crossed over the chest, holding the swords
posture.note: The posture is one of defense: the figure is closed, arms crossed, the swords held as a barrier.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of blocking. The swords are crossed, marking the card as the stalemate that will not resolve.

gaze.note: The gaze is absent. The figure is blindfolded, marking the choice as one made by not looking.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the stalemate.

centralObject.note: The swords are the central objects, the barriers of the choice. They are crossed, marking the stalemate.

heldObject.note: The swords are held. The holding is the holding of the barrier, not the weapon.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human choice, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the stalemate: the swords that are crossed.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The stalemate is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A sea and a crescent moon behind
landscape.note: The landscape is the sea and the moon: the sea is the emotion present but not the deciding factor, the moon is the intuition that is not being consulted.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open shore, not the household.

threshold.note: The sea is the threshold between the conscious and the unconscious. The figure is on the shore, not crossing.

celestialBody.note: The moon is the celestial body of the card. It is the intuition that is available but not consulted.

weather.note: The weather is clear and cool. The card is the night of the stalemate.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the figure in the centre, the swords crossed)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the stalemate, and the balance is the problem.

repetitionCount.note: The number two is the number of the pairing. The two swords mark the card as one of the contested choice.

verticalAxis.value: The moon above, the figure below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the moon to the figure. The moon is the intuition, the figure is the chooser.

horizontalAxis.value: The crossed swords across the chest
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the barrier: the swords are crossed across the chest.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright, though blindfolded.

clothing.note: The white robe marks the figure as one of purity, not of the conflict. The card is a card of the choice, not the fight.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. Her choice is mediated by her ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; she is a chooser.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of the choice, not of suffering.

binding.note: The blindfold is the binding of the card. It is the choice to not see, not the choice to be restrained.

water.note: Water is present as the sea. It is the emotion present but not the deciding factor.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of air, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the bare shore, not of the garden.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the open shore, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Two of Swords' remedy-pair is the Two of Wands: air and fire, stalemate and decision. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Two of Swords' stalemate is the Two of Wands' decision: sometimes the stalemate needs to be corrected by the willingness to choose.

prescribedAct.value: Take the blindfold off today and look at one thing you have been refusing to see.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of sight. The Two of Swords' lesson is that the stalemate is not the balance; it is the refusal to choose.

detailedReading: The Two of Swords is the air element in its phase of stalemate. Its numerical degree is two — the number of polarity and choice — and the figure is a blindfolded standing woman, holding two crossed swords, on a shore with the sea and a crescent moon behind. The landscape is the sea and the moon: the sea is the emotion present but not the deciding factor, the moon is the intuition that is not being consulted. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and the blindfold is the binding: the card is a card of human choice, not of instinct, not of suffering, and the binding is the choice to not see. The symmetry of the composition marks it as the balance of the stalemate. The prescribed act follows from this: take the blindfold off today and look at one thing you have been refusing to see. The remedy is decision — the Two of Wands — because the stalemate needs to be corrected by the willingness to choose.

name: Three of Swords
symbols: Three swords pierce a heart — the pain is specific, and it is felt.
Rain falls in the background — sorrow, in the atmosphere.
Clouds gather — grief, moving through.
There is no figure — the pain is universal, not one person's alone.

reading.upright: The Three of Swords is the specific pain of knowing: heartbreak, grief, the truth that hurts because it is true.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the healing has begun: forgiveness, the release of a pain that has been held long enough.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the three swords, the rain)
elementalRegister.note: The Three of Swords is the air element in its phase of heartbreak. The pierced heart marks it as the card of specific pain and painful truth.

numericalDegree.note: Three is the number of creation and fruition. The card is the moment at which the stalemate of the Two breaks into the pain of the Three.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Three is the first fruition of the suit's energy, in its painful form.

figureType.value: Absent (a heart pierced by three swords is the central figure)
figureType.note: There is no human figure. The card is the pure pain, not the person who feels it.

posture.note: There is no figure, so there is no posture. The card is the pain itself.

gesture.note: There is no gesture. The card is the wound, not the wounding.

gaze.note: There is no gaze. The card is the pain, not the witness.

movementDirection.value: Static (the heart is pierced, the swords fixed)
movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the wound.

centralObject.value: The heart pierced by three swords
centralObject.note: The heart is the central object, the seat of feeling. The swords pierce it, marking the card as one of specific pain.

heldObject.note: Nothing is held. The swords are not held; they are thrust in.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of pure pain, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the wound: the swords that pierce the heart.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The pain is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: Rain and clouds in the background
landscape.note: The landscape is the rain and the clouds: the sorrow in the atmosphere, the grief moving through.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open sky, not the household.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the pain, not the crossing.

celestialBody.value: The clouds (the source of the rain)
celestialBody.note: The clouds are the celestial body of the card. They are the atmosphere of the sorrow.

weather.note: The weather is rainy. The card is the grey day of the heartbreak.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the heart in the centre, the swords radiating)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the wound, though not the balance of the comfort.

repetitionCount.note: The number three is the number of fruition. The three swords mark the card as one of the specific pain.

verticalAxis.value: The swords pierce from above and below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the wound: the swords pierce the heart from above and below.

horizontalAxis.value: The swords radiate from the heart
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the piercing: the swords radiate from the heart.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The heart is upright, though pierced.

clothing.note: There is no clothing. The card is the bare heart, without the mediation of culture.

nudity.note: There is no body. The card is the heart itself, not a person.

crown.note: There is no crown. The card is the pain, not the authority.

wound.note: The wound is the central mark of the card. The heart is pierced by three swords.

binding.note: There are no chains. The card is the wound, not the restraint.

water.note: Water is present as the rain. It is the sorrow that falls on the wound.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of air, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the bare sky, not of the garden.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the sky, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Three of Swords' remedy-pair is the Three of Cups: air and water, heartbreak and celebration. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Three of Swords' heartbreak is the Three of Cups' celebration: sometimes the wound needs to be corrected by the willingness to be with others.

prescribedAct.value: Let yourself feel one specific pain today, and let it be specific.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of grief. The Three of Swords' lesson is that the pain is not the enemy; the refusal to feel it is.

detailedReading: The Three of Swords is the air element in its phase of heartbreak. Its numerical degree is three — the number of fruition — and the card is a heart pierced by three swords, with rain and clouds in the background. There is no figure, no creature, no tool other than the swords, no written word, and no binding: the card is the pure pain, not the person who feels it, and not the restraint. The wound is the central mark of the card. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the wound. The prescribed act follows from this: let yourself feel one specific pain today, and let it be specific. The remedy is celebration — the Three of Cups — because the wound needs to be corrected by the willingness to be with others.

name: Four of Swords
symbols: A figure lies on a tomb-like bed — rest, but a rest with a sword beside it.
Three swords on the wall, one beneath the bed — the conflict is suspended, not finished.
A stained-glass window — the quiet is beautiful, and it is a chosen enclosure.
The figure's hands are folded — the body has agreed to stop.

reading.upright: The Four of Swords is deliberate rest: the recuperation that must be taken, the retreat that restores.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the rest is refused or has ended: restlessness, burnout, or a return to action before the body has recovered.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the swords on the wall, the tomb-like bed)
elementalRegister.note: The Four of Swords is the air element in its phase of rest. The swords on the wall mark it as the card of recuperation and the chosen retreat.

numericalDegree.note: Four is the number of structure and stability. The card is the moment at which the heartbreak of the Three is stabilized into the rest of the Four.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Four is the stabilization of the suit's energy, in its restful form.

figureType.value: A recumbent human figure on a tomb-like bed, hands folded
figureType.note: The figure is human and still. His recumbence marks the card as one of rest, and the tomb-like bed marks the rest as one that resembles death.

posture.value: Lying on the bed, hands folded, eyes closed
posture.note: The posture is one of complete rest. The hands are folded, the eyes are closed, the body has agreed to stop.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of stillness. The hands are folded, marking the figure as one who has set aside the work.

gaze.note: The gaze is absent. The figure is not looking at the world; he is resting within it.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the rest.

centralObject.value: The tomb-like bed and the swords
centralObject.note: The bed is the seat of the rest; the swords are the conflict that has been suspended. Together they mark the card as one of chosen stillness.

heldObject.note: Nothing is held. The figure has set aside the tools of the work.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human rest, not of instinct.

tool.value: The swords on the wall and beneath the bed
tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the suspended conflict. They are set aside, not used.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The rest is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: An interior, with a stained-glass window
landscape.note: The landscape is the interior, the place of the rest. The stained-glass window marks the quiet as beautiful, and as a chosen enclosure.

architecture.value: An interior with a tomb-like bed
architecture.note: The interior and the bed are the architecture of the rest. The card is the chosen enclosure, not the open world.

threshold.note: The interior is the threshold between the conflict and the return. The figure is within it, not crossing it.

celestialBody.value: The stained-glass window (the light of the interior)
celestialBody.note: The window is the celestial light of the interior. It marks the rest as one blessed by a higher light, not one abandoned by it.

weather.note: There is no weather. The card is the interior of the rest.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the figure in the centre, the swords arranged)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the rest, though not the balance of the activity.

repetitionCount.value: Four swords (three on the wall, one beneath the bed)
repetitionCount.note: The number four is the number of structure. The four swords mark the card as one of the settled, suspended conflict.

verticalAxis.value: The swords on the wall above, the figure below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the swords to the figure. The swords are above, the figure is below, and the conflict is suspended.

horizontalAxis.value: The figure lies across the bed, the swords to the side
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the rest: the figure lies across the bed, the swords are to the side.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is recumbent, not inverted.

clothing.note: The robe is the mark of the rest. The figure is dressed as one who is prepared to be still.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. His rest is mediated by his ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; he is a rester.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of rest, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to rise.

water.note: There is no water. The card is a card of the interior, not of the sea.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of air, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the interior, not of the garden.

stone.value: The tomb-like bed and the walls
stone.note: Stone is present as the bed and the walls, the architecture of the rest.

polarity.note: The Four of Swords' remedy-pair is the Four of Cups: air and water, rest and withdrawal. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Four of Swords' rest is the Four of Cups' withdrawal: sometimes the rest needs to be corrected by the deeper withdrawal into the self.

prescribedAct.value: Lie down today and let yourself rest without needing to earn it.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of rest. The Four of Swords' lesson is that the rest is not the laziness; it is the recuperation that makes the return possible.

detailedReading: The Four of Swords is the air element in its phase of rest. Its numerical degree is four — the number of structure and stability — and the figure is a recumbent man on a tomb-like bed, hands folded, eyes closed, with three swords on the wall and one beneath the bed, in an interior with a stained-glass window. The landscape is the interior, the place of the rest. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human rest, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the rest. The prescribed act follows from this: lie down today and let yourself rest without needing to earn it. The remedy is withdrawal — the Four of Cups — because the rest needs to be corrected by the deeper withdrawal into the self.

name: Five of Swords
symbols: A figure gathers swords, smiling — the win, but the smile is not reassuring.
Two figures retreat in the distance — the cost, borne by the losers.
Clouds gather — the atmosphere is the aftermath, not the contest.
The winner is alone — the victory has emptied the field.

reading.upright: The Five of Swords is the conflict that has become a win at any cost: victory that leaves no ground to stand on.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the fight is being left: reconciliation, the willingness to stop, or the recognition that the win was not worth it.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the gathered swords, the clouds)
elementalRegister.note: The Five of Swords is the air element in its phase of empty victory. The gathered swords and the retreating figures mark it as the card of the win at any cost.

numericalDegree.note: Five is the number of the human figure and of disruption. The card is the moment at which the rest of the Four is broken by the conflict of the Five.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Five is the disruption of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A standing human figure gathering swords, and two retreating figures
figureType.note: The winner is the figure of the empty victory; the retreating figures are the cost. The two together mark the card as one of the empty win.

posture.value: Standing, one figure gathering swords, two retreating
posture.note: The posture is one of victory, but a victory that has emptied the field.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of gathering, and the smile is not reassuring. The card is a card of the win that has cost too much.

gaze.value: Looking at the swords, or at the retreating figures
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the aftermath. The winner is looking at the swords and at the losers, not at the field.

movementDirection.note: The movement is retreat. The card is the aftermath of the contest, not the contest itself.

centralObject.note: The swords are the central objects, the spoils of the empty victory.

heldObject.note: The swords are gathered, held as spoils. The holding is the holding of the win, not of the weapon.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human conflict, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the win: the swords that have been gathered.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The aftermath is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A shore or open ground with clouds above
landscape.note: The landscape is the shore or open ground, the aftermath of the contest. The clouds mark the atmosphere as one of aftermath, not of contest.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open ground, not the household.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the aftermath, not the crossing.

celestialBody.note: The clouds are the celestial body of the card. They mark the atmosphere as one of aftermath.

weather.note: The weather is cloudy. The card is the grey day of the aftermath.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the winner to one side, the retreating figures to the other)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the aftermath, not the balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number five is the number of the human figure. The five swords mark the card as one of the spoils of the empty victory.

verticalAxis.value: The clouds above, the figures below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the clouds to the figures. The clouds are the atmosphere, the figures are the aftermath.

horizontalAxis.value: The winner to one side, the retreating figures to the other
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the aftermath: the winner and the losers are separated.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright, though the field is emptied.

clothing.note: The varied dress marks the figures as distinct persons, not a uniform. The card is a contest of different claims.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their aftermath is mediated by their social positions.

crown.note: There is no crown. The winner has not been crowned; he has only gathered the spoils.

wound.value: Absent (the wound is the loss, not the body)
wound.note: There is no visible wound, but the loss is the injury. The card is the wound of the empty victory.

binding.note: There are no chains. The losers are free to retreat.

water.value: The shore or a body of water in the background
water.note: Water is present as the shore. It is the aftermath of the contest, not the water of the healing.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of air, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the bare ground, not of the garden.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the open ground, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Five of Swords' remedy-pair is the Five of Cups: air and water, conflict and grief. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Five of Swords' empty victory is the Five of Cups' grief: sometimes the win needs to be corrected by the recognition of what it has cost.

prescribedAct.value: Walk away from one fight today that you cannot win cleanly, and let the walking away be the victory.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of the leaving. The Five of Swords' lesson is that the win is not the same as the ground; some wins leave nothing to stand on.

detailedReading: The Five of Swords is the air element in its phase of empty victory. Its numerical degree is five — the number of the human figure and of disruption — and the figures are a standing man gathering swords, smiling, and two retreating figures, with clouds above. The landscape is the shore or open ground, the aftermath of the contest. There is no creature, no written word, and no binding: the card is a card of human conflict, not of instinct, and not of restraint. The loss is the central mark of the card. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as an aftermath, not a balance. The prescribed act follows from this: walk away from one fight today that you cannot win cleanly, and let the walking away be the victory. The remedy is grief — the Five of Cups — because the empty victory needs to be corrected by the recognition of what it has cost.

name: Six of Swords
symbols: A figure sits in a boat, face turned forward — passage, underway.
A ferryman poles them across — help is being given.
Six swords stand upright in the boat — the past is being carried, not left behind.
A far shore ahead — the destination is known, though not yet arrived at.

reading.upright: The Six of Swords is the passage: movement from one shore to another, the carrying of what must be carried, the leaving of what must be left.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the boat has stalled or turned: stuck on the water, unresolved baggage dragged back, or the return to what was being left.

elementalRegister.value: Air (Swords; the boat, the swords, the crossing)
elementalRegister.note: The Six of Swords is the air element in its phase of passage. The boat and the swords mark it as the card of the deliberate crossing.

numericalDegree.note: Six is the number of harmony and balance. The card is the moment at which the aftermath of the Five is resolved into the crossing of the Six.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Six is the resolved passage of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A seated human figure in a boat, with a ferryman poling
figureType.note: The passenger is the figure of the crossing; the ferryman is the figure of the help. The two together mark the card as one of passage.

posture.value: Seated in the boat, face turned forward
posture.note: The posture is one of passage: the passenger is seated, facing forward, not looking back.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of being carried. The passenger is not rowing; the ferryman is.

gaze.value: Facing forward, toward the far shore
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the passage. The passenger is looking at the destination, not at the shore left behind.

movementDirection.value: Forward (the boat moves across the water)
